# The object-listing target — verification record

*This file records the blind scan pass over the 18 object pages of the 90.05
listing, PDF pp. 199 to 216 (M4-1 chunks A2 to A8). One section per page. It
records what a reader measured on the page scan, and what that measurement
changed.*

The target is `test/fixtures/90.05-object-listing.target`. It is scaffolding:
the golden is the oracle of record, and chunk B7 deletes the target
(`docs/design/m4-codegen.md` M4-8 as amended).

## The method

Each page goes to one reader whose only source is the page scan. The reader
does not open the manual conversion, the target, or any golden. A reader
counts the page's rows before transcribing, and records blanks as well as
values, because a sweep that counts only values misses a row.

The comparison against the target is plain code, never the reader.

A disagreement takes one of two routes:

- The target is wrong. The correction goes into
  `tool/object_listing_target_source.dart` and this file records it.
- The conversion is wrong. It becomes an erratum candidate in
  `docs/HANDOVER.md`, which waits for Jack's authorization and blocks no
  other page.

## Listing page 21 — PDF p. 212

**Content: confirmed, with no change.** All 55 content lines agree with the
transcription in all six fields — LOC, OCTAL, CNTRL, the label or the `+n`
offset, the mnemonic, and the operand. The comparison found zero
disagreements.

**Geometry: confirmed.** The reader measured this page's own ink runs against
x = 429 at pitch 9.2412 px, and found the M4-8 columns: a single-digit offset
at columns 41 to 42 and a two-digit offset at 40 to 42, so the offset is
right-aligned ending at 42; both labels (`BOND.END` and `SEARCH`) at column 34;
mnemonics at 49; operands at 56. Both labelled lines print no offset, and the
offset counter restarts at `+1` on the line after the second label.

**Blank lines: corrected.** The page prints **two** blank lines between its
head and its first content line. The transcription holds one. The reader
measured the body line pitch at 15.2407 px and the gap from the head's glyph
rows to the first content row at 46 px, which is 3.02 line slots and therefore
two empty slots. It swept rows 194 to 229 at three ink thresholds and found
only a guide rule. There is no interior blank line: the 55 slots run unbroken.

The target now carries two blank lines here.
`tool/object_listing_target_source.dart` holds the measurement, and the
conversion waits for Jack (`docs/HANDOVER.md`).

**A hypothesis this raises, not yet a finding.** M4-8 records that the
transcription holds one blank line after every object page head except
PDF p. 208, where the M4-20 item (e) measurement found two. This page makes
two of two measured pages that print two. If the remaining sixteen also print
two, the transcription flattened a two-line gap everywhere it was not
separately corrected. Chunks A3 to A8 settle it. Nothing in the target assumes
it.

**A second open question, recorded and not answered.** `m1-front-end.md` M1-16
states that every page of the listing carries 55 content lines after its head,
across all 25 printer pages. This page carries 55 lines of text *plus* two
blank lines. Either the 55 counts text lines alone on the object pages, or the
M1-16 count needs qualifying. One page cannot settle it.

**Uncertain glyphs, all resolved on the ink.** The reader read a defective `0`
as `0` in LOC, OCTAL and CNTRL, where the field admits no `C`, and never
"corrected" a `C` in a mnemonic, label, or operand. The eleven doubtful glyphs
were resolved at 10x to 24x: `0074` and `0604` in OCTAL against clean prints of
the identical words elsewhere on the page; `10001` in CNTRL twice; `RQL` by its
opcode 4773 and a clear print of the same instruction; `TRA*` by its indirect
flag digits `60`; `PI)1,2` against the `I` of `LDI` and `TXI` on the same page;
and `BL)` twice against the `8` of `CP)+58`. Nothing on the page was
unreadable, and the file holds no `?`.

**A form the field description does not cover.** Two lines print `3.RS)1` — a
period inside a prefixed name. Both carry address 01643, so the two agree. The
conversion notes already record this form (`1.RS)0`, `2.RS)0`, `3.RS)1`) as
verified letter by letter.

**One flaw in this pass, recorded.** The reader's instructions carried a sample
record built from real values of this page — LOC 01327 with `TRA SYS)267,0,0`
and its octal word — taken from `docs/design/m4-codegen.md` M4-20 item (c).
That line was therefore not read blind. The contamination is bounded to one
line of 55, the reader corroborated it independently (`SYS)267` carries address
00413, which is 267 decimal) and read its CNTRL and offset differently from the
sample, and item (c) is itself a dedicated scan measurement of that same line
at 8x to 40x. Every later page prompt uses an invented sample.
